title: Football and the 2026 World Cup: A Simple Guide

cover.alt: Football fans celebrate together in a bright stadium.

blocks.title: Introduction
paragraphs: The 2026 FIFA World Cup is finished. Spain won it. Spain beat Argentina 1–0 after extra time in the final on 19 July 2026. Football has simple rules, and this World Cup had a new format.

items.prompt: Do you like football? Do you watch big tournaments?
items.answer: Open answer. For example: Yes, I like football. I watched the World Cup on TV.
items.explanation: There is no wrong answer. Just share your idea.

items.prompt: How many teams do you think play in the World Cup?
items.answer: Open answer. For example: I think about 30 or 40 teams play.
items.explanation: There is no wrong answer. Make a guess.

items.prompt: Can you name one country that is very good at football?
items.answer: Open answer. For example: Brazil is very good at football. Spain is also very good.
items.explanation: There is no wrong answer. Just name a country you know.

blocks.title: Part 1: What Is the World Cup?
paragraphs: The FIFA World Cup is a football tournament. Teams from around the world play against each other. One team wins and becomes world champion.
A football match has two teams. Each team has up to eleven players. One player on each team is the goalkeeper. The match has two halves of 45 minutes each. The team that scores more goals wins.

images.alt: Two football teams and their goalkeepers stand on the pitch.

blocks.title: Check: What Is the World Cup?

items.prompt: How long is one half of a football match?
items.explanation:
A standard match has two halves of 45 minutes each, making 90 minutes in total.

Do you think 90 minutes is a long time to watch a match? Why or why not?

blocks.title: Part 2: The 2026 Tournament
paragraphs: The 2026 World Cup was different from older tournaments. For the first time, 48 teams played. That is more teams than ever before. There were 104 matches in total.
Three countries hosted the tournament together: Canada, Mexico, and the United States. The tournament started in June 2026 and the final was on 19 July 2026.

images.alt: A map highlights Canada, Mexico, and the United States.

items.prompt: How many teams played in the 2026 World Cup?
items.answer: 48 teams played in the 2026 World Cup.
items.explanation:
This was more teams than in any World Cup before 2026.

Three countries hosted the 2026 World Cup together. Can you name them?

blocks.title: Part 3: The Final Match
paragraphs: The final match was on 19 July 2026 in New York/New Jersey. Spain played against Argentina. It was a very close match. After 90 minutes the score was 0–0, so the teams played extra time.
In extra time, Spain scored one goal. Spain won 1–0. Spain became the 2026 World Cup champions. Argentina did not score.

images.alt: Spain celebrates the 2026 World Cup win as the scoreboard shows Spain 1-0 Argentina.

items.prompt: Who won the 2026 World Cup final, and what was the score?
items.answer: Spain won the final. The score was 1–0. Spain scored in extra time.
items.explanation:
Spain beat Argentina 1–0 after extra time and became world champions.

How do you think the Argentina players felt after the match?

blocks.title: Part 4: Extra Time and Goals
paragraphs: Sometimes a match ends 0–0 or with the same score after 90 minutes. This is called a draw. In a final, there must be a winner. So the teams play extra time — two more short halves.

If the score is still equal after extra time, the teams use a penalty shoot-out. Each team takes turns kicking the ball from the penalty spot. In the 2026 final, Spain scored in extra time, so there was no penalty shoot-out.

items.prompt: What happens if the score is the same after extra time in a final?
items.answer: The teams use a penalty shoot-out to find the winner.
items.explanation:
In the 2026 final there was no penalty shoot-out because Spain scored in extra time.

Would you find a penalty shoot-out exciting to watch? Why?

items.prompt: Spain won the 2026 World Cup. Why was the tournament special? Would you fix it or change anything next time?
items.answer: It was special because 48 teams played and three countries hosted it. Spain won the final 1–0 against Argentina after extra time. I would make travel easier for fans.
items.explanation: Good answers use facts from the lesson. You can also add your own idea.
